ROLL CALL: At 6:36 p.m., on Monday, January 22, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
PRESENT via videoconference:  ANDRADE-STADLER
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

COUNCIL BUSINESS

  video/teleconference at the January 22, 2024 City Council meeting due to medical reasons.

  her at her location.

2.  COMMENDATIONS: WINNERS OF THE 2023 HOLIDAY HOME DECORATING
  CONTEST – F2M24-3

  Mayor Maza and the Alhambra City Council, on behalf of the citizens of Alhambra, wished to
  recognize and congratulate the winning contestants from the City’s 2023 Holiday Home
  Decorating Contest. This contest invited residents to show their sense of community and
  holiday spirit through the use of holiday decorations on their homes. The winners are to be
  commended for displaying extraordinary efforts in enhancing and promoting a family-oriented
  community through their colorful and imaginative holiday displays. Director of Parks and
  Recreation MACIAS delivered a presentation on the winning homes, which is on file in the
  City Clerk’s office. Mayor MAZA presented commendations to the winners of the 2023 Holiday

3.  COMMENDATIONS: SPARK OF LOVE TOY DRIVE – F2M24-3

  Mayor Maza and the Alhambra City Council, on behalf of the citizens of Alhambra, wished to
  recognize and thank the Alhambra Fire Department team who were instrumental to the
  success of this year’s Spark of Love Toy Drive. Their leadership and organization allowed the
  City to serve over 600 families during the holiday season. Because of their efforts, children
  and families were able to experience the love and care of their community and share the joy
  of the season. The City Council deeply appreciated the efforts of the Fire Department staff
  and all of the event’s participants who allowed the City to continue the toy drive, a wonderful
  tradition to serve families in our community. Mayor MAZA presented commendations to the
  Fire Department team that worked so diligently to make the event a success.

PUBLIC HEARING

4.  PUBLIC HEARING TO CONSIDER ADOPTION OF URGENCY ORDINANCE REGULATING
  MEDICINAL CANNABIS DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS – F2M23-78, N2M24-6, O2M23-
  4824, O2M24-4825

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M24-6 for the City Council to hold a public
  hearing to consider adoption of an Ordinance extending Ordinance No. O2M23-4824, an
  interim urgency ordinance to implement California law governing medicinal cannabis
  delivery-only retailers, for a period of 10 months and 15 days. City Attorney MONTES delivered
  a staff report. The California Legislature adopted Senate Bill 1886 (“SB 1186”) in 2022, entitled
  the Medicinal Cannabis Patients’ Right of Access Act, which precludes cities and counties
  from adopting or enforcing regulations that prohibit or have the effect of prohibiting the retail
  sale of medicinal cannabis by delivery. SB 1186 took effect on January 1, 2024. The City
  Council adopted Ordinance No. O2M23-4824 at its December 11, 2023 meeting establishing
  interim urgency regulations implementing. This ordinance is set to expire on January 25, 2024.
  The proposed ordinance would extend the term of Ordinance No. O2M23-4824 for ten months
  and fifteen days in accordance with Government Code Section 65858, unless earlier repealed.
  An ordinance adopting permanent regulations was prepared and the Planning Commission
  recommended Council adoption of the ordinance. City staff intended to notice this ordinance
  for a public hearing at the City Council after the Council took final action on the proposed
  comprehensive Zoning Code update.

  Open & Close Public Hearing:  Mayor Maza opened the public hearing, and as there
  was no one who wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. MONTES discussed the
  ordinance in the context of the zoning code update and the taxes collected from the point of
  sale. Councilmember PÉREZ also requested more information from staff regarding the point
  of sale of the cannabis businesses and the location of grow houses or warehouses near
  Alhambra.

  Action Taken: City Council adopted the following urgency ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M24-4825: An Urgency Ordinance of the City Council of
  the City of Alhambra, California, extending the term of Ordinance No.
  O2M23-4824, an Interim Urgency Ordinance to implement California law
  governing medicinal cannabis delivery-only retailers within the City

  after which such ordinance shall go into effect immediately.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MAZA

5.  CHAMBER OF COMMERCE UPDATE – F2M21-43

  Alhambra Chamber of Commerce President, Mr. John BWARIE, presented an update for
  Chamber of Commerce activities from March 2023 to December 2023.

  Discussion: Council expressed their appreciation to the Chamber of Commerce for their
  continued work to support local businesses. Vice Mayor PÉREZ and Mr. BWARIE discussed
  the possibility of a food hall to showcase small food vendors who could not afford brick and
  motor restaurant spaces, the success of Gallery Nucleus, and the effort to bring in new
  businesses to reinvigorate Valley Boulevard. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER
  discussed finding grant opportunities, Council’s ability to work with the Chamber, and re-
  examining the key demographics of interest in Alhambra. Councilmember LEE discussed
  finding a book store for Alhambra, complaints from small businesses regarding high utility
  costs and high operational costs, efforts to retain existing businesses, returning the Lunar New
  Year celebration to Valley Boulevard, and attracting small businesses. Mayor MAZA
  emphasized the need to continue a strong relationship between the Chamber of Commerce
  and the City government.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 13)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, except Item Nos. 7, 9, 10, and 13, were considered by the
City Council to be routine were enacted by one motion.

6.  APPROVAL TO AMEND CONTRACT FOR PARKING HEARING OFFICER SERVICES –
  F2M24-16, K2M18-385, M2M24-11

  On January 1, 2019, the City entered into an agreement (K2M18-385) with Joseph Malette to
  conduct Parking Hearing Officer services for two years in an amount not to exceed $45,000.
  The term of the agreement had been amended to extend the term through June 30, 2024;
  however, there had not been an increase to the contract amount. The proposed amendment
  for an additional $30,000 would result in a total contract amount of $75,000. The services
  under this contract were highly specialized; therefore, amending the contract would be in
  accordance with the provisions cited under section 3.38.050 for the Alhambra Municipal Code.
  The proposed amendment also extended the term of the agreement through June 30, 2027.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to the agreement between the Joseph
  Mallette and the City of Alhambra for ongoing Parking Hearing Officer services, not to exceed
  an additional $30,000 through June 30, 2027; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-11)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER

 7.  AWARD CONTRACT & APPROPRIATE FUNDS: PYROTECHNICS SERVICES FOR THE
  ALHAMBRA FOURTH OF JULY CELEBRATION – F2M23-75, RFP2M23-27, C2M24-6,
  M2M24-12

  On November 13, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) for Pyrotechnics Services for the Alhambra 4th of July Celebration. On November 27,
  2023, the Parks & Recreation Department received one proposal in response to the RFP. The
  3-year proposal received was $120,000 (2024 for $40,000, 2025 for $40,000 and 2026 for
  $40,000). An expenditure in the amount of $20,000 for the 2024 fireworks show must be
  approved for the City to enter into a contract with Garden State Fireworks, Inc. The total
  expenditure would be charged to multiple fiscal years.

  Public Comment:  Jennifer NG, S. Cordova St., suggested that the City needed to
  reexamine the scale of the fireworks show due to the negative environmental impact on the air
  quality.

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE recalled previous discussions regarding restrictions on
  fireworks in Alhambra. Councilmember MALONEY clarified that the item referred specifically
  to the fireworks show for the July 4th celebration. City Attorney MONTES stated that he would
  report to Council regarding the Alhambra Municipal Code sections referring to fireworks. Vice
  Mayor PÉREZ recommended looking into drone shows for future celebrations. Mr. MALONEY
  referred to environmental concerns with fireworks and discussed contract provisions if larger
  government agencies further restrict firework displays in the next few years. Mayor MAZA
  reported on his research into drone shows and stated that while currently drone shows were
  too expensive for the City’s budgeted event, he expressed hope that it might be achievable
  one day.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Garden State Fireworks, Inc. in an amount not to
  exceed $40,000 in 2024, $40,000 in 2025 and $40,000 in 2026 for the annual 4th of July
  Celebration; instruct the Director of Finance to pay 50% of this year’s costs ($20,000 for 2024)
  in FY 2023-24 and pay the remainder of the $40,000 as an expenditure in FY 2024-25 in
  account number 101.60.6110.66314; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-12)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded: LEE
  Ayes:  LEE, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE

9.  AWARD CONTRACT: DESIGN SERVICES FOR PREPARATION OF ADAPTIVE
  TRAFFIC/TRAFFIC RESPONSIVE UPGRADES PROJECT - PHASE 1 – F2M23-47,
  RFP2M23-17, C2M24-8, M2M24-14

  The City was awarded funding through the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
  Authority (LACMTA) for four traffic signal improvement projects within the City of Alhambra
  (Project ID# MR 1.3.2.01 Atlantic, MR 1.3.1.02 Fremont, MR 1.3.1.01 Garfield, and MR
  1.3.2.06 Valley). The City released a Request for Proposals (RFP) and received four proposals
  for the preparation of Phase 1 of the City’s Adaptive Traffic/Traffic Responsive Control
  Systems Project. Following an extensive selection process, staff selected Advantec Consulting
  Engineers, Inc. as the most qualified consultant for this work. Staff requested the City Council
  approve an agreement with Advantec Consulting Engineers, Inc., in an amount not to exceed
  $231,008. Phase 1 consisted of the development of the preliminary design concepts of traffic
  elements and identification of actual locations for the project. Phase 2 consisted of the
  preparation of actual engineering designs and plans, estimates, and specifications for
  implementation of all improvements as developed in Phase 1. The Project was located along
  the four major corridors of Atlantic Boulevard, Fremont Avenue, Garfield Avenue and Valley
  Boulevard. There were 62 signalized intersections along these four corridors.

  Public Comment:  Lewis MCCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the contract as it
  would relate to the Active Transportation Plan and the suggestions for crosswalks.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Advantec Consulting Engineers, Inc. in an amount not
  to exceed $231,008 to prepare Phase 1 of the City’s Adaptive Traffic/Traffic Responsive
  Control Systems Project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M24-14)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded: LEE
  Ayes:  LEE, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA

  Strategic Plan planning session with the City Council, staff and a consultant was tentatively

  2040), GENERAL PLAN MAP AMENDMENT AMD-23-07 (AN AMENDMENT TO THE CITY
  OF ALHAMBRA GENERAL PLAN LAND USE MAP), AND INITIAL STUDY/NEGATIVE
  DECLARATION – F2M20-24, O2M23-4823, R2M23-54

  After receiving staff’s presentation and public testimony at the November 13, 2023 public
  hearing and then continuing the public hearing to the December 11, 2023 meeting, the City
  Council deliberated and determined which of the Planning Commission’s recommendations to
  include and gave first reading to Ordinance No. O2M23-4823 approving Zoning Text
  Amendment AMD-23-10 (The Comprehensive Update to the City of Alhambra Zoning Code
  [Title 23 of the Alhambra Municipal Code]) and Zoning Map Amendment AMD-23-09 (An
  Amendment to the City of Alhambra Official Zoning Map). Additionally, the Council deliberated
  and determined which of the Planning Commission’s recommendations to include in a
  Resolution approving General Plan Text Amendment AMD-23-08 (An Amendment to the Land
  Use and Community Design Chapter of the City of Alhambra General Plan, Vision 2040),
  General Plan Map Amendment AMD-23-07 (An Amendment to the City of Alhambra General
  Plan Land Use Map), and adopting the Initial Study/Negative Declaration for the Project
  pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). At the January 8, 2024 Council
  meeting, after further deliberation, the Council made further revisions to the Ordinance and
  Resolution. The Council then gave first reading to Ordinance No. O2M23-4823. Staff
  requested that the City Council introduce O2M23-4823 for its second reading and adopt the
  ordinance as well as adopt the related Resolution (R2M23-54).

  The staff reports and attachments from all previous Planning Commission and City Council
  presentations on the Zoning Code, including the staff report and attachments prepared for the
  public hearings on November 13th and December 11th, are available through the project
  website at: https://www.alhambracodeupdate.com/participate.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS – F2M24-4

1) Jennifer NG, S. Cordova St., spoke regarding the Bike and Pedestrian Plan and reminded the City
  to review the intersection at S. Cordova and Main St. She also discussed the Historic Preservation
  Ordinance and requested temporary protections for existing historic homes in Alhambra until the
  final ordinance would be adopted.

2) Sharif SHAKHSHIR, 416 N. Bushnell Ave., spoke regarding the current conflict between Israel
  and Palestine. He requested Alhambra support a resolution for cease fire, discontinue providing
  financial aid to Israel, and consider adopting Bethlehem as a Sister City.

3) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova Ave., spoke regarding the Zoning Code Update and the
  ongoing need for public engagement. He also spoke regarding Mr. Shakhshir’s comments and
  the history of conflict in the Middle East.

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS (ANNOUNCEMENTS & FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS) – F2M24-7

Councilmember LEE reported on the 2023 actions of the Alhambra Historical Society, as the Council
representative to the Historical Society. She stated that she would continue to update Council on
upcoming events from the Alhambra Historical Society.

Vice Mayor PÉREZ spoke regarding public comment received by Mr. Shakhshir and discussed the
conflict between Israel and Palestine as well as the effects in the United States. She supported a cease
fire. Mayor MAZA also referred to Mr. Shakshir’s comments and echoed Ms. Pérez’s sympathy. He
stated that a number of cities in California had drafted resolutions calling for a cease fire. He requested
Council’s consideration of an agendized Resolution calling for a cease fire between Israel and
Palestine. Ms. LEE requested more information about the resolution given the delicacy of international
affairs, expressed concerns regarding prejudice against Alhambra residents, and requested language
encouraging support for peace and not assign blame to any side. She supported agendizing a
discussion. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER expressed caution in seeming to take any side in
the conflict and requested that any resolution focus on peace in general given the negative effects on
all people in the Middle East. Councilmember MALONEY echoed the sentiment of neutrality and that
the resolution support the people in the region rather than the specific governments. Mr. MAZA clarified
his intention for a resolution calling for a general ceasefire. Ms. PÉREZ supported an agendized
discussion of a resolution and supported Ms. Lee’s suggestions to address ongoing prejudice
experienced in the United States because of the conflict. She also suggested the resolution call for the
release of hostages held by Hamas and call for a cease fire.

Mayor MAZA announced upcoming events in Alhambra such as the Lunar New Year Festival,
upcoming public meetings regarding the Active Transportation Plan, and upcoming public meetings
regarding the Sustainability Plan. He further reported on his attendance at the National Mayors
